chapters.title: Building e-document applications on e-document core
Receiving e-documents and importing purchase invoices
Error handling and alternative import options
Roadmap, localization strategy and access points

features.name: E-Document Core App
features.description: A global extension for all countries that provides the foundation for electronic invoicing capabilities across Business Central. It will be used in W1 and all country localizations, packaging common e-document functionality including interfaces for creating and importing documents, integrating with endpoints, background jobs, field mapping logic, error handling, logging, and retention policies.
caveats: Not 100% fit for all file formats and requirements initially
Local flavors and specific localizations will be added on top

features.name: Electronic Invoicing
features.description: A core functionality enabling continuous transaction control and real-time invoicing reporting to authorities. The first release focuses on invoicing with plans to continue with other documents.
caveats: First release focuses on invoicing primarily
Other document types to follow later

features.name: Two-Corner Model
features.description: Direct communication between sender and receiver for electronic invoices. Involves creating an electronic document and sending it via email or other means without a service provider intermediary.
caveats: Works in countries where direct communication is voluntary
Too simple for countries requiring service provider involvement

features.name: Three-Corner Model
features.description: Communication via a service provider where the sender delivers documents to the service provider who then delivers to the receiver. Requires specific format and API communication with the service provider.
caveats: Requires specific format for service provider
More complex than two-corner model

features.name: Four-Corner Model
features.description: Model where sender and receiver both have access points that communicate with each other and government authorities. Sender delivers to their access point, which communicates with receiver access point, which delivers to receiver.
caveats: Most complex model requiring access points on both sides
Can send additional file formats to customer beyond government requirements

features.name: E-Document Messaging System
features.description: An asynchronous service handling message exchange between access points. Handles initial confirmation of document receipt, approval or rejection responses from customers, and delivery of status messages back to the sender.
caveats: Requires asynchronous implementation
Handles complex multi-stage message flow between parties

features.name: E-Document Global Service App
features.description: An additional app to be provided by Microsoft ready to connect with third-party access points. Based on e-document core and designed to provide minimum 80% of required features.
features.status_evidence_quote: we will soon provide additional e doent global app ready to connect with a third party services this have will be based on our
caveats: Coming soon, not yet released
Will provide minimum 80% of required features

features.name: Local E-Document Localizations
features.description: Country-specific implementations built on top of the e-document core. Can include file format specifications, service integrations, and new tables and fields as required by local regulations.
caveats: Scope varies by country requirements
Not limited to the three example countries shown

features.name: Partner Extensibility Framework
features.description: Partners can extend the e-document core app and Microsoft localizations with additional features including industry-specific functionality and new capabilities.
caveats: Technical documentation to be provided in following period

features.name: Third-Party Access Point Integration
features.description: Third-party access point providers will be able to extend e-document features. Different providers have different feature sets which Microsoft does not plan to deliver directly.
caveats: Each access point provider has different feature sets
Microsoft will not deliver provider-specific features

features.name: E-Document Service setup
features.description: Allows configuration of document services with document formats, service integrations, batch processing support, import parameters, and field mapping rules for transforming exported and imported documents.

features.name: E-Document Workflow
features.description: Workflow functionality to define events and responses for e-documents, including when documents are created and which service to send them to, with support for multiple service destinations.

features.name: Document Sending Profile
features.description: Configuration that specifies which e-document service flow to use for documents, enabling electronic document processing for customers.

features.name: E-Document status tracking
features.description: Real-time status view for e-documents in the processing pipeline, with detailed service-level status, logs showing chronological events, mapping details, and communication logs between Business Central and services.

features.name: Manual e-document actions
features.description: Options to manually send, recreate, cancel, or get approval for e-documents when automatic processing encounters errors, allowing recovery from service issues.

features.name: E-document receiving via background job
features.description: Automated receiving of e-documents through background job processing, which pulls documents from configured receiving endpoints and automatically creates purchase invoices with field mapping from external documents.

features.name: Import electronic documents to purchase invoice
features.description: Receive e-documents and automatically create purchase invoices from them, with automatic mapping of items based on item references.
caveats: Only for creating new purchase orders, not updating existing ones
Item mapping required or must use alternative mapping methods

features.name: Error handling with item references
features.description: When an item cannot be found during import, the system shows an error and allows bypassing it by mapping text to accounts instead of items.
caveats: GUI must allow viewing errors
Manual remapping required when items not found

features.name: Import to journal lines
features.description: Alternative option to create journal lines instead of purchase invoice documents when needed, with mapping of vendor charges to specific accounts.
caveats: Requires manual configuration of vendor to account mapping

features.name: Sales invoices to e-invoices
features.description: Create electronic invoices from sales invoices and sales orders for sending.

features.name: Credit memo handling
features.description: Electronic document handling for credit memos from both sales and purchase side.

features.name: Configurable local features and messages
features.description: E-document features are configurable at local level; basic features in global app but most configuration and messaging depends on local market requirements.
caveats: Local functionality required for country-specific features

features.name: Update existing purchase orders
features.description: Planned feature to update existing purchase orders with partial invoices from e-documents.
caveats: Not available in current release

features.name: Third-party access points app
features.description: New app on top of e-document core for third-party access point communication, planned for end of year.
features.status_evidence_quote: we are preparing this third party access points app it will be already until the end of this year as a new app on
caveats: Separate app from core e-document functionality

features.name: Country-specific localizations
features.description: E-invoicing localizations for multiple countries based on local enforcement dates and regulatory requirements.
caveats: Delivery depends on country enforcement dates
Not all countries confirmed yet

features.name: Access point provider options
features.description: Customers and partners can choose which certified access point provider to use based on country requirements; Microsoft provides integration with third-party certified providers.
caveats: Access point certification requirements vary by country
Some countries provide uncertified endpoints, others require certified services
